data.title: Worried about AI bubble burst? Invest in this sector instead
data.description:
Investors questioning the returns on artificial intelligence (AI) spending should consider securing exposure to another sector: US homebuilders.

Housing stocks charged higher on Thursday as Treasury yields declined, offering a glimpse of how they stand to benefit from a rotation out of technology due to AI bubble concerns.

D.R. Horton, Lennar, and PulteGroup all posted “strong intraday gains” as investors reassessed an industry battered by expensive financing.

The attraction goes beyond a rotation: sustained mortgage-rate relief could improve affordability for buyers and reduce the financial concessions builders need to close sales.

Homebuilder stocks to benefit from lower mortgage rates

Housing offers a concrete way to invest in falling borrowing costs. Freddie Mac reported Thursday that the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate slipped to 7.32% from 7.40% a week earlier.

That remains rather expensive, but the direction matters for households whose purchasing decisions depend heavily on monthly payments.

For homebuilders, a sustained decline could deliver two benefits – more qualified buyers and less pressure to subsidize financing.

Mortgage-rate buydowns help move inventory, but they consume money as well that could otherwise support profitability.

The opportunity therefore extends beyond stronger sales volumes.

Homebuilders could eventually retain more profit on each closing as affordability improves.

However, one weekly decline doesn’t establish a recovery, and mortgage rates need not follow Fed policy moves precisely.

A different earnings driver can diversify an AI-heavy portfolio

US homebuilder stocks offer material exposure to household formation, employment, and housing affordability, giving investors a different set of earnings drivers from the companies financing the AI infrastructure boom.

The sector’s current difficulties also explain its recovery potential.

October’s NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index fell to 29, while 43% of builders reported cutting prices and 65% offered sales incentives.

Those figures reveal notable operating pressure that easing financing conditions could gradually relieve.

Still, investors should distinguish a rotation opportunity from a dependable hedge. An AI sell-off accompanied by widespread job losses could undermine housing demand even as bond yields fall.

The strongest backdrop would be moderating inflation and stable employment: enough economic resilience to support purchases, alongside lower borrowing costs.

Selective exposure makes more sense than assuming every housing-related business will benefit equally.

D.R. Horton stock: a top pick within US homebuilders

D.R. Horton (NYSE: DHI) stands out because its national scale and broad product offering provide multiple avenues to capture improving demand.

America’s largest builder by volume operates across 126 markets in 36 states, reducing dependence on any single local housing economy.

Its mortgage-financing business also gives it tools to address buyers’ affordability constraints.

Its latest reported quarter demonstrates resilience: fiscal Q3 closings increased 4% to 23,983 homes, generating $9.2 billion in consolidated revenue and $904.9 million in net income.

Nevertheless, cancellations increased to 20% from 17% a year earlier, underscoring continued buyer hesitation.

That combination makes Horton a credible recovery candidate with an established earnings base.

Its October 29 results will provide the next test: investors should watch incentives, cancellations, and margins before treating Thursday’s rally as evidence of a lasting turnaround.

data.title: Dow falls 1.25% as oil tops $117 and investors await Fed, big tech earnings
data.description:
US stocks ended lower on Friday as losses spread beyond technology shares, while rising oil prices and renewed concerns over the US-Iran conflict added pressure to markets.

Investors also looked ahead to a busy week of corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve's upcoming interest-rate decision.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.25%, or about 659 points, to 52,209.16.

The S&P 500 declined 0.52% to 7,623.86, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.21% to close at 25,955.34.

Despite Friday's declines, the Dow gained 0.4% over the week. The S&P 500 fell 0.5%, while the Nasdaq lost 0.7%.

Oil prices rise as Middle East tensions weigh on stocks

Energy prices climbed as renewed concerns about the conflict involving the US, Israel and Iran raised the risk of further disruption to Middle Eastern oil supplies.

West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 3.8% to settle at $103.34 a barrel, while Brent crude gained 3.25% to $116.85. Brent's settlement was its highest since April.

The rally followed reports that the US and Israel could be preparing plans for renewed attacks on Iran.

Iran has indicated that it is prepared to retaliate, adding to uncertainty over the conflict's potential impact on energy markets.

The energy sector reached a record high on Friday, making it a notable exception to the broader market weakness.

However, higher oil prices also raised concerns about inflation and the potential pressure on household spending.

University of Michigan data showed US consumer sentiment slipped close to a record low in October as rising prices linked to the Middle East conflict weakened households' views of the economy.

Dow stocks fall as weakness spreads beyond technology

Selling pressure extended across several sectors on Friday, including consumer staples, utilities and healthcare.

Financial stocks also weakened, contributing to the Dow's decline.

American Express fell more than 3% after announcing plans to reduce its global workforce by about 5%, citing preparations for the growing use of artificial intelligence.

Caterpillar declined around 2%, while Goldman Sachs lost more than 1%.

Telecommunications stocks also came under pressure following a report that SpaceX was seeking access to thousands of cellular sites as it explores plans to become a fourth nationwide wireless carrier.

Technology shares were comparatively resilient after the previous session's sell-off.

Microsoft edged higher, while Micron Technology gained 2.5% and Advanced Micro Devices rose 1.7%.

Investors have been reassessing the outlook for AI-related stocks amid concerns about the scale of borrowing required to finance data centres and the potential impact of higher interest rates.

However, recent corporate earnings have provided some support for the sector.

The 10-year US Treasury yield rose more than four basis points to around 4.999% on Friday, returning above the 5% level after briefly falling below it a day earlier.

Fed decision and Big Tech earnings in focus

Investors are preparing for a significant week of corporate results and monetary policy developments.

About one-third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report quarterly earnings next week, including Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon.

Their capital expenditure forecasts will be closely watched for indications of whether spending on AI infrastructure will continue to expand at its current pace.

LSEG IBES data indicated that S&P 500 companies were on track to increase earnings by more than 32% in the third quarter, supporting the broader market's gains this year.

The Federal Reserve is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged at its Wednesday meeting.

Investors will nevertheless look for signals about whether policymakers could raise rates in December.

Markets are also monitoring the November 3 US midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress.

Together, corporate earnings, interest-rate expectations and geopolitical risks could shape the direction of US stocks in the coming week.

data.title: Evening digest: oil jumps to $117, SpaceX to enter wireless services
data.description:
Oil prices surged amid fresh Middle East supply concerns, while Anthropic expanded its European AI ambitions, SpaceX explored a nationwide wireless service, and SK Hynix shelved plans for a US listing of its Solidigm unit.

Oil prices rise as Houthi attacks fuel supply concerns

Oil prices climbed on Friday, with Brent crude touching its highest level in nearly six months as Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia heightened concerns about disruptions to Middle Eastern energy supplies.

Brent crude futures rose 3.7%, to $117.37 a barrel, after reaching an intraday high of $117.45. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 4.45%, to $103.91.

Brent was on track for a weekly gain of 6%, while WTI was set to finish the week 1.5% higher.

The rally followed attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi rebels across Saudi Arabia, including on energy infrastructure.

Saudi Aramco ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran on Thursday, Reuters reported.

Supply concerns were compounded by an oil spill detected off the UAE coast near Umm Al Quwain. Authorities had not identified the tanker involved or disclosed the cause.

Shipping security also remained a concern, with October emerging as the worst month for attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waterways, according to data cited by Reuters.

Anthropic launches AI consultancy venture in Europe

Anthropic is expanding its enterprise AI business through a partnership with London-based private equity firm Hg, according to the Financial Times.

The companies plan to establish an independent consultancy that will place AI consultants and engineers within businesses to help integrate artificial intelligence into existing workflows and develop new products.

The venture is expected to begin operations by the end of 2026, with London and Berlin as its main hubs.

Anthropic will contribute capital from its balance sheet, while Hg will invest through the funds it manages.

The arrangement combines Anthropic's AI technology and engineering expertise with Hg's experience in software and services businesses.

The move puts Anthropic in more direct competition with traditional IT consultancies.

The company has already entered the US AI implementation market through Ode, an independent AI services company introduced in July.

The European expansion comes as Anthropic prepares for a potential initial public offering.

SpaceX explores nationwide wireless expansion

SpaceX shares rose 1.84% on Friday as the company reportedly pursued access to at least 80,000 cellular sites across the United States.

According to Bloomberg, the company is in talks with cellular infrastructure providers as it seeks to combine Starlink's satellite connectivity with ground-based infrastructure and expand into nationwide wireless services.

Crown Castle is among the companies involved in the discussions, alongside American Tower and Vertical Bridge Holdings. Potential agreements could be worth billions of dollars.

The initiative could help SpaceX move closer to becoming a fourth nationwide wireless carrier.

The company recently received Federal Communications Commission approval to launch 15,000 satellites designed to connect directly to mobile phones.

The report also affected established telecom stocks. AT&T shares fell about 7.9% in trading, while Verizon declined around 1.18% and T-Mobile lost approximately 7.71%.

SK Hynix shelves Solidigm's potential US IPO

SK Hynix shares rose 4.05% on Friday after the South Korean chipmaker abandoned plans to pursue a potential US IPO of its subsidiary Solidigm.

In a regulatory filing, SK Hynix said it had halted its review of a possible listing and discussions about pre-IPO investment, citing recent capital market conditions.

Solidigm had reportedly been preparing an offering that could raise around $10 billion and value the business at as much as $100 billion.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley had reportedly been selected to work on the proposed transaction.

Established in 2021 following SK Hynix's acquisition of Intel's flash memory business, Solidigm supplies high-capacity solid-state drives used in AI data centres.

The proposed listing also faced scrutiny from South Korean regulators over concerns about minority shareholder dilution and the implications of listing a subsidiary separately in the US.

The decision comes amid wider efforts in South Korea to address the so-called “Korea discount”, in which domestic companies often trade at lower valuations than international peers.

data.title: Why are AMD, Intel stocks gaining today?
data.description:
AMD and Intel stocks rose on Friday, rebounding after a sector-wide sell-off a day earlier as investors returned to select technology shares despite weakness across the broader market.

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) gained 2%, while Intel was up 1.76%. Technology stocks advanced as investors assessed the outlook for artificial intelligence spending and semiconductor demand ahead of the upcoming earnings season.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.10%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.42% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 1.09%.

Technology gained 0.43%, making it the second-best-performing S&P 500 sector behind energy, which advanced 2.50%.

Only two of the S&P 500's 11 sectors traded higher.

Intel's Arizona Fab expansion draws analyst attention

Intel was also in focus after Wedbush Securities highlighted the potential contribution of additional manufacturing capacity to the company's revenue growth.

Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson said the installation of equipment at Intel's Fab 62 facility in Arizona was consistent with expectations that production would begin in 2028.

However, he noted that it remained unclear whether the initial production lines would use Intel's 18A or 14A process technology.

Bryson said additional capacity was important because existing constraints were limiting Intel's ability to meet customer demand, particularly for Xeon server processors.

In his view, these constraints were also weighing on revenue growth and the company's ability to optimise its product mix.

Intel Foundry CTO and COO Naga Chandrasekaran said this week that construction and equipment installation were underway at Fab 62, the company's sixth high-volume manufacturing facility at its Ocotillo campus in Arizona.

Operations are expected to begin by the end of 2027, although Intel has not disclosed which manufacturing node the facility will use or its planned production capacity.

Intel has also reported progress at other US facilities.

Its plant in New Albany, Ohio, received its first major structural truss, while its Oregon development fab integrated a High-NA extreme ultraviolet lithography machine.

AI demand supports server chips as PC market weakens

Susquehanna updated its price targets for several semiconductor companies ahead of earnings season, reflecting differing expectations across the sector.

The firm raised its AMD price target to $620 from $550 and increased its Qualcomm target to $185 from $160. However, it lowered Intel's target to $105 from $115.

Susquehanna analyst Christopher Rolland said artificial intelligence would likely drive much of the semiconductor sector's potential upside, while the broader industry upcycle continued.

Rolland noted that semiconductor lead times had expanded by approximately two weeks for a second consecutive quarter in the firm's SemiSIGnals data.

He also highlighted increasingly aggressive pricing, including a 12% quarter-on-quarter increase in the third quarter of 2025, with further price increases expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and into 2027.

However, the PC market outlook has weakened.

Rolland said third-quarter original design manufacturer builds were tracking significantly below previous expectations, pointing to potentially below-seasonal second-half results for AMD and Intel's client businesses.

Both companies are shifting wafer capacity from PC processors towards server products to address demand associated with agentic AI.

Rolland said the scale of potential server growth would depend on how quickly additional capacity becomes available.

He also noted that Arm-based hyperscale CPUs were expected to gain share as host processors for custom AI accelerators, while memory supply constraints could weigh on smartphone demand.

Meanwhile, expanding hyperscaler capital expenditure plans continued to support data centre demand, although power and infrastructure constraints raised questions about how much planned capacity could be delivered.

data.title: Why are Micron, SK Hynix, and SanDisk stocks climbing on Friday?
data.description:
Micron, SK Hynix and SanDisk shares traded higher on Friday as a rebound in the broader semiconductor sector lifted investor sentiment following a technology-led selloff in the previous session.

Micron MU gained more than 3%, while SK Hynix rose over 4% and SanDisk advanced 1.4%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, also known as the SOX, climbed more than 1% as chip stocks recovered from Thursday's losses.

The rebound followed a sharp pullback in technology shares on Thursday as investors assessed the implications of rising borrowing costs and heavy corporate debt issuance for artificial intelligence and other technology investments.

The SOX fell 6.7% on Thursday, its worst daily performance since June 23, while Micron lost about 6%.

SK Hynix's decision to abandon plans for a US initial public offering of its Solidigm business also supported sentiment toward memory-chip stocks on Friday, with analysts pointing to potential implications for future NAND flash supply.

Solidigm IPO cancellation eases supply concerns

The planned Solidigm IPO had been expected to raise as much as $15 billion and value the business at roughly $150 billion.

Its cancellation was viewed as shareholder-friendly for SK Hynix because the company will retain full exposure to Solidigm's growth potential.

The decision has also shifted investor attention toward SK Hynix's third-quarter earnings release, due later this month, when management is widely expected to announce enhanced shareholder return commitments.

For Micron and SanDisk, the cancellation could have implications beyond investor sentiment.

According to LYNX Equity Strategies, the IPO would have provided Solidigm with capital to finance additional NAND manufacturing capacity in the United States.

That expansion could have increased global supply in three or more years, potentially putting pressure on NAND prices and competing suppliers.

In an October 23 note, the analyst team led by KC Rajkumar said the scrapped IPO removes a potential source of funding for future capacity expansion.

"The overhang of new capacity addition to the global supply of NAND flash has been eliminated," LYNX wrote.

The firm said the development would ordinarily represent a material positive for Micron and SanDisk, both suppliers of NAND flash memory, because slower capacity growth could support industry pricing and valuations.

However, it cautioned that broader market conditions could limit the impact on share prices.

Analysts divided over semiconductor weakness

Market strategists offered differing assessments of the recent decline in semiconductor shares.

Chris Verrone, chief market strategist at Strategas, told CNBC that the weakness appeared technical rather than fundamental, suggesting any further pullback could be short-lived.

“Fundamentally, we’re seeing great strength, but technically, there’s some pressure on these semiconductors, and if the pressure continues, it could take the market on a little leg lower, which I think will be quick and a great buying opportunity,” he said.

However, John Mowrey, chief investment officer at NFJ Investment Group, took a more cautious view of memory stocks and the South Korean market, which is heavily exposed to the sector.

Micron outlook remains positive for some analysts

DA Davidson maintained a positive outlook on Micron after attending a webcast focused on the company's upcoming innovations and competitive position in the memory market.

Managing director and technology research head Gil Luria said the company's technological advantages were not fully reflected in its valuation.

“We see Micron as having a leadership position in memory technology, with far wider moats than are implied by the current valuation,” Luria said in a note on Wednesday.

The firm reiterated its Buy rating and $3,000 price target.

“Memory is integral to the AI product,” Luria wrote, adding that greater memory content and bandwidth could allow AI systems to operate at a higher level.

DA Davidson also highlighted Micron's presence across three key memory technologies: dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), NAND and high-bandwidth memory (HBM).

data.title: S&P 500 eyes 4th straight year of double-digit gains, a rare feat in 100 years
data.description:
US stocks may have seen immense volatility lately but they are heading into the final quarter of 2026 after a strong run, with the S&P 500 on track for a fourth consecutive year of double-digit gains, according to BlackRock Fundamental Equities.

Such a streak has occurred only three times in the past 100 years, it says.

Carrie King, managing director and global chief investment officer of BlackRock Fundamental Equities, said historical patterns suggest a strong first three quarters more often precede further gains than a reversal during the final quarter.

The fourth quarter has also typically been the strongest period of the year for US equities.

However, King said investors must assess the specific economic and market conditions shaping the outlook rather than rely solely on historical trends.

Four questions are particularly relevant as investors position their portfolios for the remainder of 2026: whether artificial intelligence spending is generating returns, how long earnings growth can continue, where opportunities are emerging beyond AI and which international markets offer attractive prospects.

AI investment begins to show returns

BlackRock sees evidence that the enormous investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure is beginning to generate financial benefits.

The firm's Global Technology team estimates that AI computing infrastructure investments by hyperscalers and AI cloud providers can now achieve payback in less than three years, compared with periods of up to four years just months ago.

Revenue growth at major cloud providers accelerated in the second quarter, with the growth rate twice that of the year-earlier period.

This suggests businesses are increasingly using AI services, helping justify continued investment in computing capacity.

The spending requirements remain substantial.

AI infrastructure investment is estimated to exceed $10 trillion by 2030 as demand for AI tokens and the computing power needed to generate them expands.

The benefits are also spreading beyond infrastructure providers.

The number of large-cap US companies citing AI-related financial improvements increased by 77% over the past year, according to the figures cited by BlackRock.

That trend suggests companies adopting AI are beginning to realise productivity gains, improve competitiveness and generate additional revenue, potentially sustaining the next phase of investment.

Earnings growth could support equities into 2027

Corporate earnings provide another source of support for the market outlook.

Consensus estimates point to the third consecutive year of double-digit earnings growth for the S&P 500 in 2026, a run not seen in two decades.

Early forecasts suggest the streak could extend into 2027.

Longer-term expectations are also elevated.

Five-year forward earnings growth estimates stand at 18%, compared with a historical average of 12%, according to BlackRock.

The outlook is constructive outside the US as well.

Europe is recording its strongest earnings growth in three years, while emerging markets are forecast to deliver earnings growth of nearly 50% in 2026.

South Korea and Taiwan, both beneficiaries of AI-related demand, are expected to contribute significantly to that performance.

The breadth of earnings growth matters because it could help reduce reliance on a narrow group of large technology companies to drive equity market returns.

Cyclical sectors offer opportunities beyond AI

BlackRock also sees a cyclical recovery developing in the US, creating opportunities in sectors that are not directly tied to artificial intelligence.

Industrials, financials and non-AI analogue semiconductors are showing signs of improvement.

While companies supplying equipment and services for AI data centres have attracted considerable investor attention, King sees improving earnings prospects in traditional cyclical businesses, including logistics, airlines and packaging.

Analogue semiconductor companies could benefit from an industrial recovery and improving inventory cycles.

Financial companies also have several potential tailwinds.

Major US banks are benefiting from investment banking, trading and capital markets activity, alongside subdued loan delinquencies and a recovery in loan growth from depressed levels.

Consumer finance companies could see earnings accelerate as credit conditions normalise, funding costs decline and consumer spending remains resilient.

These areas offer investors opportunities to participate in broader economic growth without concentrating their exposure entirely in AI-related stocks.

Japan and Europe provide diversification

Outside the US, BlackRock is particularly interested in Japan and Europe, which have delivered strong equity performance without relying on the same scale of AI investment driving US markets.

Japan's year-to-date return stood at 21%, compared with gains of around 13% for both the US and Europe, according to the figures cited by BlackRock.

The country is undergoing structural reforms supported by government and corporate initiatives. BlackRock's Japan team also finds that a substantial proportion of Japanese stocks continue to trade below book value, potentially creating opportunities for investors.

Specialty materials companies supplying the AI infrastructure buildout are another area of interest.

In Europe, improving earnings are being led by the energy sector.

The region has a greater share of companies positioned to benefit from rising investment in energy and infrastructure associated with AI development.

European companies also generate a significant portion of their revenue outside the continent, providing exposure to a broader range of economic drivers.

BlackRock sees European equities as a way to complement US technology-heavy portfolios, with European stocks trading at a 25% discount to their US counterparts.

BlackRock favours a risk-aware approach

Despite the constructive outlook, King cautioned that investors must remain alert to geopolitical uncertainty, Federal Reserve policy, the effects of higher interest rates on long-duration assets and the sustainability of earnings growth beyond AI.

The combination of elevated market expectations and concentrated investment in certain themes makes diversification and stock selection particularly important.

BlackRock's position is to remain constructive on equities while acknowledging that volatility could persist through the fourth quarter and beyond.

The firm believes an active, fundamentals-driven investment approach can help investors navigate market fluctuations while seeking opportunities across sectors and regions.

data.title: Crude oil price forecast as Brent hits $117 amid US-Iran war fears
data.description:
Crude oil prices continued their bull run, reaching its highest level since May as concerns about the escalation between the US and Iran grew. It jumped to $117, continuing a bull run that started in July when it bottomed at $70. This rally will likely continue rising in the coming weeks.

Brent and WTI jumps on rising US-Iran escalation fears

There are signs that the US, Iran, and Israel are planning a major escalation in the coming weeks. 

President Donald Trump has insisted that the US will not launch any attacks against Iran before the midterm election. 

Media reports suggest that the US and Israel are preparing a massive attack aimed at Iran’s civilian infrastructure. Trump and his officials believe that such a move will push Iran to capitulate and reach a deal. 

Israeli leaders have also planned to attack Iran’s oil infrastructure, a move meant to choke the country’s finances. A key target in these attacks will be Kharg Island, which handles more than 90% of Iran’s oil exports.

Iran, on the other hand, has warned that its response to any attacks will be more severe than before. It has warned that it will target energy infrastructure of its neighboring countries, including Bahrain, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. 

Most analysts believe that the next phase of the war will be more destructive than previously. For one, Houthis, a less-equipped group than Iran has demonstrated its capability in choking Saudi Arabia’s oil facilities. 

Crude oil prices also continued rising as investors reacted to the ongoing Iranian attacks on ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz. The UKMTO issued a report of a ship that was attacked by an unknown projectile today, but open-source information is that more ships were attacked. 

Brent crude oil price technical analysis

Crude oil price chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that Brent has been in a strong rally in the past few months. This rally started after it bottomed at $70 in July. It has now crossed the important resistance level of $109.96, which coincided with the highest swing on September 11. Moving above that level was important as it invalidated the double-top pattern. 

Crude oil has remained above the ascending trendline that links the lowest swings since July. It also rose above the 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA), while top oscillators like the MACD and the Relative Strength Index (RSI) have continued rising. 

Therefore, the price will likely continue rising as bulls target the key resistance level of $120. It may even rally past that as the crisis in the Middle East escalates.

data.title: Rubrik stock hits a record high on AI demand, as a risky pattern slowly forms
data.description:
Rubrik’s stock extended its strong rally on October 23, reaching a record high as demand for cybersecurity solutions continues to grow amid the ongoing AI boom. Shares of RBRK jumped to $129.60, a 210% gain from their lowest point this year, lifting the company’s market capitalization to $26.9 billion. However, the stock appears to be forming a rising wedge pattern, which suggests it could pull back soon.

Rubrik stock jumps as demand for services rise

RBRK stock has been one of the best-performing stocks as the ongoing AI boom has led to a surge in demand for cybersecurity products. This demand has grown in the era of AI agents, which are expected to be the biggest threats in the world. 

The most recent results showed that its business continued to boom in the second quarter, with revenue rising by 38% to $427.3 million. Its subscription revenue rose by 37% to $407 million, a trend that the management expects will continue. 

Its customers paying at least $100,000 a year rose to 3,084, a 23% annual increase. Some of the biggest customers are companies like PepsiCo, Iron Mountain, and Adobe.

Analysts believe that the company has more room for growth. The average estimate among analysts is that its third-quarter revenue will be $430 million, up by 22% from a year earlier. Its guidance for the fourth quarter is expected to be $446 million, up by 18% from the same period last year.

Analysts are generally bullish on RBRK stock

Top analysts tracking Rubrik have a bullish outlook for the company. Dan Ives, who started Yorkville Ives, initiated the company with a target of $145, suggesting a 12% jump from the current level. 

Shrenik Kothari, a Baird analyst, boosted his rating to outperform, while Wedbush’s Steven Wahrhaftig has a target of $120.

The challenge, however, is that the stock has jumped above most of the analysts’ target. The average target among analysts is $115, suggesting a 12% drop from the current level. 

A major risk that Rubrik faces is its high valuation multiple. It has a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 240, much higher than the technology sector median of 21. Its forward EV-to-EBITDA stands at 227, also higher than the median of 13.

Rubrik stock technical analysis

RBRK stock chart | Source: TradingView

On the charts, we see that the RBRK stock has been in a strong upward trend in the past few months. It has jumped from a low of $41.73 in January to the current $130. The stock jumped above the key resistance level of $92.26, its highest point in December last year.

It has remained above the 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA), which has provided it with a strong dynamic support. The stock also remains above the Supertrend indicator. 

These technicals suggest that the stock has more upside to go. Such a move may push it to the resistance level of $150. The risk, however, is that the stock has formed a rising wedge pattern, which is made up of two ascending and converging trendlines. 

Rubrik’s MACD indicator has also formed a bearish crossover pattern. Therefore, there is a possibility that the stock will rise a bit, and then retreat as investors start booking profits.

data.title: Why Nvidia stock is in red today: growth case meets bearish warning
data.description:
Nvidia stock NVDA traded down 0.2% on Friday after falling 4.4% in the previous session, as investors weighed contrasting views on the chipmaker’s long-term prospects.

Seaport Research Partners reiterated a bearish rating, citing competitive pressures and financial commitments, while Laffer Tengler Investments CEO Nancy Tengler argued that Nvidia could still double in value over the next five to 10 years, even if earnings growth slows.

Jay Goldberg, an analyst at Seaport Research Partners, maintained a Sell rating and a $180 price target, below Nvidia’s Thursday closing price of $212.

He acknowledged that the company was positioned to deliver record sales in the near term but warned that challenges could become more significant over the following year.

Nvidia’s shares have climbed sharply in recent years, making it the world’s most valuable publicly traded company.

However, concerns about the sustainability of artificial intelligence spending have recently weighed on chipmakers and other AI-linked stocks.

Seaport flags competition and financial commitments

Goldberg identified four main risks to Nvidia’s outlook, including data centre construction constraints, financial commitments, circular financing and tensions involving smaller cloud infrastructure providers.

Although around 55 gigawatts of data centre capacity has been announced for the coming year, Goldberg said the industry may struggle to build more than 30 gigawatts because of shortages of electricians, gas turbines and utility connections.

He also warned that Nvidia’s commitments to securing its supply chain and supporting data centre construction total about $250 billion.

That figure excludes obligations connected to a funding initiative being developed with Wall Street, which Goldberg said could expand from $500 billion to $1 trillion.

Nvidia has the financial capacity to support these commitments, according to Goldberg, who expects operating cash flow to reach $200 billion this year.

However, he argued that such obligations could amplify the impact of a downturn.

Goldberg also raised concerns about Nvidia investing in and lending money to suppliers and customers.

He said credit guarantees and other financial support could effectively reduce customers’ costs, raising questions about underlying demand and competitive pressures.

Neocloud exposure creates strategic tension

Goldberg highlighted Nvidia’s relationship with neocloud providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius, which offer computing capacity as a service.

He argued that Nvidia benefits from having numerous smaller customers rather than relying on a few large cloud providers with greater bargaining power.

However, those smaller companies have taken on substantial debt amid uncertainty about the profitability of AI infrastructure.

“If the neoclouds fail to lift off, that doubles back on Nvidia with reduced sales and even more reduced margins,” Goldberg said.

He acknowledged that Nvidia could continue benefiting from strong demand in the near term, adding that the longer-term risks could take time to materialise.

Tengler sees room for further growth

Tengler offered a more optimistic view, arguing that Nvidia could double over five to 10 years even if earnings growth eventually slows to 20% or 30%.

She cited earnings growth of 96% and said she expected it to decelerate to 70% the following year before potentially settling at a slower pace.

These figures represent her outlook rather than company guidance.

Tengler compared Nvidia’s potential trajectory with Microsoft’s Azure cloud business, saying slower growth had not prevented the business from supporting the stock’s performance.

She also said Nvidia traded at a 13.5 earnings multiple when her firm added it to its value portfolio earlier in the summer.

That valuation reference was historical, not current.

data.title: Moderna leaked data was positive, what's hurting MRNA stock then?
data.description:
Moderna’s (MRNA) leaked cancer-vaccine trial results looked “promising” on the surface, yet the biotech stock came under intense pressure late on Thursday and was weak on Friday morning too, although the stock regained the losses and was trading higher later in the session.

In fact, MRNA slipped through its 20-day moving average (MA) this week, indicating bears have taken back control of the near-term.

Despite recent weakness, however, Moderna stock remains a blockbuster investment for 2026, currently trading at more than 6x its price at the start of this year.

Why Moderna stock keeps sliding?

The Phase 3 leaked trial data showed that “intismeran autogene” – Moderna’s personalized cancer vaccine – combined with Merck’s Keytruda reduced the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42% versus Keytruda alone.

It also lowered the risk of distant metastasis or death by 38%. Those are meaningful clinical gains, and the companies reported no new safety signals.

But the market had already rewarded the study’s success following August’s initial announcement.

The detailed findings therefore needed to improve expectations further.

Bloomberg reported that analysts questioned whether the melanoma results justified confidence in a much broader cancer franchise.

For MRNA shares, that distinction matters – demonstrating that one treatment works supports its development, while supporting a premium valuation requires a credible path to commercial revenue across a larger market.

Earlier trial created a difficult comparison

Another pressure point was the apparent gap with earlier research.

A smaller study showed a 49% reduction in recurrence or death and a 59% reduction in distant metastasis or death, compared with 42% and 38%, respectively, in the larger trial.

However, “different patient populations” and “follow-up periods” mean these are not really direct comparisons.

The latest findings also contain nuance that headline percentages miss.

The companies said the treatment groups performed similarly during the first six months; a prespecified analysis showed stronger benefits afterward. Overall survival data remain immature.

That makes sweeping conclusions premature. The study supports a reduction in recurrence, but it has not yet established an overall survival benefit.

Moderna investors assessing durability, treatment timing, and eventual adoption still have major questions to resolve as follow-up continues.

What’s the next test for MRNA shares?

Moderna’s next challenge is turning clinical progress into an economically attractive product.

The company is preparing to seek US approval and anticipates a potential launch in 2027.

Because the therapy is tailored to each patient’s tumor, investors will need to assess manufacturing capacity, delivery times, reimbursement, and the cost of supplying treatment.

Strong efficacy alone cannot establish the margins or sales volumes the business will ultimately generate.

Friday’s decline therefore raises a practical valuation question: how much future success does MRNA stock already assume at about 50x sales?

Regulatory progress, launch economics and evidence from additional cancer trials could help answer it.

Until then, a positive melanoma study can strengthen Moderna’s scientific credentials while still leaving shareholders vulnerable to falling expectations.
